newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds slightly higher, uncertain mood.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds slightly higher, uncertain mood.

text.p: Argentine bonds finished slightly higher Monday after a slow session in which traders awaited U.S. economic indicators and were loath to predict a clear market trend.

"This market is dead," said a trader at a local bank, adding that the market remains unwilling to find a clear trend as long as uncertainty remains over U.S. interest rates. With the U.S. Employment Cost Index due Tuesday and key jobless figures due later in the week, uncertainty is set to rise in coming days, traders said.
Argentina's FRB Brady bond due 2005 rose 1/8 to 91-1/8.
The dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 was up 0.01 at 126.01.
The slight firmness in the market "mostly comes from local banks and some shorts," said another trader.
But, "foreign funds are holding cash, waiting for U.S. indicators," he added as an explanation for the slim, directionless trade seen in recent weeks.
In the money markets, call money rates rose to 5.23 percent from 5.13 percent.
